# Fewer sequential steps: draft verification versus learned iteration

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/foundation-models/generation-paths.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-11 · 16 topic entries / 7 representative comparisons

Speculative decoding exchanges cheap proposals for expensive verification batches, preserving the target distribution with exact correction. Diffusion language models and data-space refinement instead change generation paths or training objectives. Ask who determines the final distribution, what each step does and keeps, and whether NFE or acceptance length becomes actual speed.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Parallel proposals need not change the target distribution

Exact speculative decoding tolerates weak drafts because target verification and residual correction determine the distribution. Windowed-MTP compresses draft access, mainly risking acceptance and speed. Medusa proposes via backbone heads but its exactness depends on sampling and verification, not the tree itself. The key boundary is whether verifier history and rules are preserved.

Sources: [Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding](../../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en.md) · [Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context](../../../../reproductions/2607.21535-windowed-mtp/README-en.md) · [Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads](../../../../reproductions/2401.10774-medusa/README-en.md)

### Iterative steps have different dependencies

DQwen3.5 uses masked denoising. PUMBA lets earlier carry affect later loss, while Data-Space Iteration refines under fixed noise without gradients through the prefix rollout. Compare states, conditions, and gradient spans before cost, and use task-appropriate language or image metrics rather than one step count.

Sources: [dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en.md) · [On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2609.37974-pumba/README-en.md) · [Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration](../../../../foundation-models/2610.12102-data-space-iteration/README-en.md)

### Changing generative conditions differs from scheduling an existing decoder

dQwen3.5 modifies a hybrid attention/RNN backbone for bidirectional conditioning and masked-denoising training. B3 schedules overlapping blocks in an already compatible diffusion model; it does not supply that model. Its block-causal mask prevents the current block from reading a future draft, but does not eliminate future self-editing or prove full target-distribution preservation like exact speculative correction. Backbone, sampler and gate need separate validation.

Sources: [Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.14387-b3/README-en.md) · [dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why does shrinking Windowed-MTP's draft window make a different quality promise than shrinking the target window? {#cross-draft-window-versus-target-window}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Exact verification can preserve the original full-history target distribution despite changed proposals, provided correction is proper. Shrinking target history changes its conditional law. A cheaper draft can reduce acceptance, so divide combined draft and verification cost by actual accepted output.

    **Illustrative example:** A full-history target can correct a draft that forgot an early name; a truncated target may not see the name either.

    Sources: [Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context](../../../../reproductions/2607.21535-windowed-mtp/README-en.md) · [Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding](../../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en.md)

### Why are Medusa future-token proposals and DQwen3.5 multi-position denoising not the same parallel generation? {#cross-future-heads-versus-denoising}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Medusa proposes candidates for backbone verification, while DQwen3.5 learns bidirectional masked denoising with different conditioning and objectives. Specify sampling, training investment, and quality criteria; parallel position count does not establish equivalent output laws.

    **Illustrative example:** Propose three words and verify them versus fill several blanks and denoise again: parallel work, different contexts and acceptance rules.

    Sources: [Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads](../../../../reproductions/2401.10774-medusa/README-en.md) · [dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en.md)

### Why use different gradient rules for reused outputs in PUMBA and Data-Space Iteration? {#cross-carry-gradient-versus-prefix-stopgrad}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** PUMBA backpropagates through carry within its window for cross-step credit. Data-Space Iteration stops the prefix graph and updates only the selected refinement, with teacher/fake paths detached for the generator. Reuse alone does not specify gradients; swapping the rules changes memory, objective, and algorithm.

    **Illustrative example:** Detaching all PUMBA carries removes intended credit, while backpropagating through all data-space prefixes is a different recipe.

    Sources: [On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2609.37974-pumba/README-en.md) · [Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration](../../../../foundation-models/2610.12102-data-space-iteration/README-en.md)

### Does adding B3's spawn gate turn an ordinary AR model into a diffusion language model? {#cross-spawn-gate-not-diffusion-backbone}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. The gate decides when a compatible diffusion decoder may start its future block. Bidirectional/block conditioning, denoising and a self-editing sampler are still needed. dQwen3.5's architecture adaptation and masked training are a different layer that gating cannot replace.

    **Illustrative example:** A CPU gate returning True for low entropy is only a permission state. It predicts no token and does not transform fixed causal AR weights into a future-block editing model.

    Sources: [Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.14387-b3/README-en.md) · [dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en.md)
